mainTopic: The special פרשיות, interrupting the regular reading cycle, the fast-day schedule, and the holiday Torah readings
overview: The amud opens by defining the fourth special Shabbat before פסח: the Shabbat of the week in which ראש חודש ניסן falls, even if ראש חודש is on Friday. The גמרא then asks what 'we return to the order' on the fifth Shabbat means. רבי אמי says the order of weekly Torah portions, and רבי ירמיה says the order of הפטרות. אביי supports רבי אמי from the משנה 'לכל מפסיקין', since weekday special days have a Torah reading but no הפטרה. רבי ירמיה answers that on שבת the interrupted order is the הפטרות and on weekdays it is the Torah reading. The גמרא then asks why fast days interrupt the reading at all, and answers that the morning of a public fast is taken up by a communal gathering, as רב הונא said. אביי describes the fast-day schedule: the first half of the day examining the town's conduct, then a quarter for reading and a quarter for prayer, proven from verses in נחמיה and עזרא. Finally, a new משנה begins listing the Torah readings for each festival and special day, and its last entry, fast days, continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Defining the fourth special Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: The fourth special Shabbat (פרשת החודש) is the Shabbat of the week in which ראש חודש ניסן falls, even if ראש חודש falls on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which is the fourth Shabbat? Any Shabbat whose week has ראש חודש ניסן in it, even if ראש חודש falls on Friday.
steps.whatsHappening: The text explains which Shabbat counts as the fourth of the special Shabbatot before פסח, the one on which פרשת החודש is read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule depends on the week, not only on the Shabbat itself. If ראש חודש ניסן falls on Friday, the Shabbat before it still counts, because Friday is part of that Shabbat's week. So פרשת החודש is read before the month begins, not on the Shabbat after it.

keyTerms.meaning: The fourth special Shabbat, when פרשת החודש is read
The first day of the month of Nisan
Within it, meaning during that Shabbat's week

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that when ראש חודש falls on Friday, the reading moves to the Shabbat after it. The Shabbat before Friday is the one that counts.

phrases.english: And which is the fourth Shabbat?
Any one in which the New Moon of Nisan falls
to occur within its week,
and even if it falls on Friday.
phrases.notes: The 'week' here starts with that Shabbat. So when ראש חודש falls on Friday, the reading is on the Shabbat six days earlier, not the day after.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the earlier definitions of the first, second, and third special Shabbatot, which came on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fourth Shabbat is the Shabbat of the week containing ראש חודש ניסן, even when ראש חודש is on Friday.

steps.title: Which order do we return to on the fifth Shabbat?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line 'on the fifth we return to the order' and asks what 'order' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'On the fifth Shabbat we return to the regular order.' The order of what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה and asks a clarifying question about it. This sets up two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'return to the order' implies that something regular was interrupted during the four special weeks. The question is what that was: the weekly Torah portion or the weekly הפטרה.

keyTerms.meaning: We return to the regular order

phrases.english: On the fifth, we return to the regular order, etc.
To the order of what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from defining the fourth Shabbat to the next line of the משנה, about the fifth Shabbat.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which regular cycle resumes on the fifth Shabbat: the Torah portions or the הפטרות?

steps.title: First answer: the order of Torah portions
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says we return to the regular cycle of weekly Torah portions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: we return to the order of the weekly Torah portions.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers that the interrupted cycle is the weekly פרשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, on the four special Shabbatot the regular weekly פרשה is not read at all. Only the special portion is read. So on the fifth Shabbat the cycle of Torah readings resumes.

keyTerms.meaning: The cycle of weekly Torah portions

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
One returns to the order of Torah portions.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cycle of weekly Torah portions resumes, because it was fully replaced during the special weeks.

steps.title: Second answer: the order of הפטרות
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה says we return to the regular cycle of הפטרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: we return to the order of the הפטרות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives a different answer: the interrupted cycle is the הפטרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, the regular פרשה is still read on the special Shabbatot, and the special portion is added as מפטיר. Only the regular הפטרה is replaced with one that matches the special portion, so the הפטרה cycle is what resumes.

keyTerms.meaning: The cycle of readings from the Prophets

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
One returns to the order of the haftarot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אמי's answer in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הפטרה cycle resumes, because only the הפטרה was replaced during the special weeks.

steps.title: אביי supports רבי אמי from a משנה about interruptions
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רבי אמי's view is more logical and cites a משנה: 'For all special days we interrupt,' including ראשי חדשים, חנוכה, פורים, fast days, מעמדות, and יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: it makes sense to follow רבי אמי, because we learned in a משנה: for all these we interrupt the regular readings: for ראשי חדשים, חנוכה, פורים, fast days, מעמדות, and יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sides with רבי אמי and brings a משנה as his source. He explains how it proves his point in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists special days on which the regular reading is interrupted. Several of these, such as ראש חודש, חנוכה, fast days, and מעמדות, often fall on weekdays. That detail will be the key to the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense to follow his view
We interrupt (the regular order of readings)
Groups of ordinary Israelites who read Torah in their towns while their partner כהנים served in the מקדש

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It stands to reason to follow Rabbi Ami,
as we learned: for all of these we interrupt,
for New Moons, for Hanukkah, and for Purim,
for fast days, for the maamadot, and for Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אַמֵּי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between steps 3 and 4 by bringing outside support for רבי אמי.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's view that the regular cycle being resumed is the Torah portions
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'לכל מפסיקין', which lists special days, many of them weekdays, that interrupt the regular reading

steps.title: How the proof works: there is no הפטרה on weekdays
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי אמי, 'interrupting' makes sense because there is a weekday Torah reading. According to רבי ירמיה, it does not, because there is no הפטרה on weekdays.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for the one who says we return to the order of Torah portions, because there is a Torah portion read on weekdays. But for the one who says we return to the order of הפטרות, is there a הפטרה on a weekday?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why the משנה supports רבי אמי. The 'order' that gets interrupted has to be something that exists on weekdays too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the same word for interrupting on weekday holidays. On weekdays the Torah is read on Monday and Thursday, but no הפטרה is read. So the 'regular order' must mean the Torah portions, which fits רבי אמי and makes רבי ירמיה's reading hard.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי: on the fifth Shabbat the cycle of weekly Torah portions resumes. רבי ירמיה: the הפטרה cycle resumes. אביי supports רבי אמי because the 'order' interrupted on weekday holidays can only be the Torah reading, since there is no weekday הפטרה.
steps.confusionAlert: The weekday Torah reading here means the short Monday and Thursday reading from the upcoming פרשה. This is why a 'regular order' exists on weekdays at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: The proof assumes that 'the regular order' means the same thing in both משניות. That assumption is what turns a list of holidays into evidence about the special Shabbatot.

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who said:
one returns to the order of Torah portions —
this is because there is a Torah portion read on weekdays.
But according to the one who said:
one returns to the order of haftarot —
is there a haftara on a weekday?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: no, there is not.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: לְסֵדֶר פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת הוּא חוֹזֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the משנה quoted in step 5 supports רבי אמי and challenges רבי ירמיה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אמי's view, and against רבי ירמיה's
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that weekdays have a Torah reading but no הפטרה, so the 'interrupted order' in the משנה must be the Torah portions
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's reading of 'returning to the order' as the הפטרה cycle
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה speaks of interrupting the regular order on weekdays, but there is no weekday הפטרה to interrupt.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: Each case follows its own meaning
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers אביי's proof by saying the word 'order' changes meaning depending on the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי ירמיה) says: this case is as it is, and that case is as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה defends himself against אביי's proof from the משנה about 'interrupting.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argued that 'interrupting' only makes sense for the Torah-reading cycle, because weekdays have no הפטרה. רבי ירמיה replies that the list in the משנה 'לכל מפסיקין' does not refer to one cycle for every item. When a listed day has a הפטרה (when it falls on Shabbat), the interrupted order is the הפטרות. When it falls on a weekday, which has no הפטרה, the interrupted order is the Torah readings. So אביי's proof does not decide the question.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other side of the debate)
This is as it is, and that is as it is (each case has its own meaning)

steps.whatToRemember: The argument between רבי אמי and רבי ירמיה stays open. אביי's proof is deflected because 'order' can mean different things in different contexts.

phrases.english: And the other one (Rabbi Yirmeya would say):
This is as it is
phrases.notes: On days with a haftara (Shabbat), 'order' means the haftarot.

phrases.english: and that is as it is.
phrases.notes: On weekdays, with no haftara, 'interrupt' means the Torah reading order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought by אביי in steps 5-6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the weekday משנה proves what 'order' means in our משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes 'interrupt' in the משנה 'לכל מפסיקין' refers to the same cycle in every case. But on days with a הפטרה it can mean the הפטרות, and on weekdays it means the Torah readings.

steps.title: Why should fast days interrupt the regular reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why fast days need to break the regular Torah-reading cycle at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But on fast days, why do I need an interruption? Let us read the regular portion in the morning, and the fast-day portion at מנחה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's list, which includes fast days among the days that interrupt the regular order. It suggests both readings could fit into a fast day without any interruption.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fast day has two Torah readings, one in the morning and one at מנחה. So the גמרא proposes reading the regular weekly portion in the morning and the fast-day portion at מנחה. If that works, the regular cycle never has to be interrupted.

keyTerms.meaning: The regular matter (portion) of the day

steps.confusionAlert: 'עניינא דיומא' here means the regular weekly-cycle portion. It does not mean a special reading about the fast. The fast reading is called 'תעניתא.'

phrases.english: But on fast days, why do I need an interruption?
Let us read in the morning the regular portion of the day,
and at Mincha the fast-day portion!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה quoted in step 5 and questions why fast days are on its list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inclusion of fast days in the list of days that 'interrupt.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fast days have two reading slots, so both the regular portion and the fast portion could be read without breaking the cycle.

steps.title: The morning is taken up by a communal gathering
steps.stepSummary: The answer supports רב הונא, who said the morning of a fast day is used for a communal gathering.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רב הונא, for רב הונא said: in the morning there is a gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the regular portion cannot be read in the morning, because the morning of a fast day is used for a communal gathering. In doing so, the גמרא notes that our משנה supports רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a public fast, the community gathers in the morning, and the leaders examine the town's conduct. Because the morning is taken up this way, there is no regular morning reading time to use for the weekly portion. That is why fast days do interrupt the cycle. The משנה's ruling fits רב הונא's statement and backs it up.

phrases.english: This supports Rav Huna,
for Rav Huna said:
From the morning, a gathering.
phrases.notes: The community assembles to examine the town's conduct.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: the morning time slot is occupied.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both readings could fit into the day, so no interruption is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The morning is used for a communal gathering, so the regular reading cannot go there, and fast days do interrupt.

steps.title: What is done on a fast day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the community spends a public fast day.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we conduct ourselves (on a fast day)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical schedule of a fast day. This sets up אביי's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא mentioned a morning gathering. The גמרא now wants the full picture of the day: what happens in the morning, and what happens afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: How do we act? What do we do?

phrases.english: How do we act?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for details about the gathering mentioned in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The full schedule of a public fast day.

steps.title: אביי's fast-day schedule
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the first half of the day is spent examining town affairs. A quarter is spent reading Torah and the הפטרה, and a quarter is spent praying, based on a verse in נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: from morning until midday we examine the affairs of the town. From midday until evening, a quarter of the day we read the Torah and the הפטרה, and a quarter of the day we pray. As it says: 'They read in the book of the Torah of ה׳ their God a quarter of the day, and a quarter of the day they confessed and bowed down.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question with a clear schedule for the fast day and backs it up with a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The day is split in half. The first half goes to examining the community's behavior. The second half is split again: one quarter for reading Torah and the הפטרה, and one quarter for prayer and confession. The verse in נחמיה shows the 'quarter of the day' division for reading and for prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: They read the Torah and read the הפטרה

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic model for how a תענית ציבור should be run: first self-examination, then reading and prayer.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
From the morning until the middle of the day
we examine the affairs of the town.
From the middle of the day until evening,
a quarter of the day they read the Torah and the haftara,
and a quarter of the day they pray,
as it is stated: 'And they read in the book of the Torah of the Lord their God'
a quarter of the day,
and a quarter (of the day) they confessed and bowed down.'

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: First half of the day: examining the town. Second half: a quarter for reading and a quarter for prayer.

steps.title: Why not reverse the order?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: maybe the reading and prayer should come first, and the examination of the town afterward?
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe I should reverse it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's order. The verse in נחמיה shows the time divisions, but it does not say which half comes first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse only teaches 'a quarter for reading and a quarter for prayer.' It does not say whether those come before or after examining the town. So the order could just as well be flipped.

phrases.english: But perhaps I should reverse it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order in אביי's schedule from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the examination comes first and the reading and prayer come second.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse in נחמיה gives the time divisions but not their order.

steps.title: Verses in עזרא show the examination comes first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves from עזרא that the gathering over the people's sins happens until the afternoon, and prayer comes afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think that. For it is written: 'Then everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel over the sin of the exiles gathered around me, and I sat stunned until the evening offering.' And it is written: 'And at the evening offering I arose from my fast.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea of reversing the order. It brings two verses from עזרא showing that the gathering about sin came first and prayer came later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In עזרא, people gathered around him because of the community's sin, and he sat until the time of the afternoon offering (מנחה). That matches the morning examination of the town's affairs. Only then did he rise and pray, which matches the reading and prayer in the second half of the day. So אביי's order is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: It should not enter your mind (do not think that)

steps.whatToRemember: On a public fast, the first half of the day goes to examining the community's behavior. The second half goes to Torah reading and prayer, as shown by עזרא.

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind,
as it is written: 'Then there gathered around me'
everyone who trembled at the words of the God of Israel
over the transgression of the exiles,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי יוֹשֵׁב מְשׁוֹמֵם עַד לְמִנְחַת הָעָרֶב״,
phrases.english: and I sat appalled until the evening offering',
and it is written: 'And at the evening offering I arose from my fast.'
phrases.notes: Ezra 9:5. He then knelt and prayed.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The order of the two halves of the day could be reversed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verses in עזרא show that the gathering about sin lasts until מנחה, and prayer comes after it.

steps.title: The Torah readings for the major festivals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the Torah portion read on פסח, שבועות, ראש השנה, יום כיפור, and סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: On פסח we read the section about the festivals in תורת כהנים (ויקרא). On שבועות we read 'Seven weeks.' On ראש השנה we read 'In the seventh month, on the first of the month.' On יום כיפור we read 'After the death.' On the first day of סוכות we read the festivals section in תורת כהנים. On the other days of סוכות we read about the קרבנות of סוכות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a simple list matching each major festival to the Torah portion read on that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reading fits the day. It either describes the holiday itself or the special service of that day. For example, 'אחרי מות' describes the יום כיפור service in the משכן. On סוכות, the first day gets the general festivals section, and the remaining days get the section listing that festival's daily קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה.
The Torah section listing all the festivals (ויקרא 22:26–23:44).
The section describing the יום כיפור service (ויקרא 16).
The section listing the daily offerings of סוכות (במדבר 29).

steps.confusionAlert: Some of these readings are not what we read in shul today. For example, on שבועות we read 'בחדש השלישי.' The גמרא will discuss these differences later. For now, just learn what the משנה itself says.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the basis for the whole system of holiday Torah readings in shul.

phrases.english: MISHNA: On Passover they read
from the portion of the Festivals of Leviticus.
On Shavuot: "Seven weeks."
On Rosh HaShana: "In the seventh month, on the first of the month."
On Yom Kippur: "After the death."

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג קוֹרִין
phrases.english: On the first festival day of Sukkot they read
from the portion of the Festivals in Leviticus,
and on all the other days of the festival
from the offerings of the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins. It moves away from the earlier discussion of how a public fast day is divided.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each major festival has a set Torah reading connected to that day's theme or service.

steps.title: The Torah readings for the other special days
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list: חנוכה, פורים, ראש חודש, מעמדות, and then begins the entry for fast days.
steps.simpleTranslation: On חנוכה we read about the נשיאים. On פורים we read 'And עמלק came.' On ראש חודש we read 'And on your new months.' At the מעמדות we read about the creation of the world. On fast days we read...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the same list, now covering the smaller special days. The last entry, fast days, is cut off and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each reading still matches the day. The נשיאים brought gifts at the dedication of the משכן, which fits חנוכה, the rededication of the מקדש. The story of עמלק fits פורים, since המן came from עמלק. Those in the מעמדות prayed for the קרבנות, which hold up the world, so they read about Creation.

keyTerms.meaning: The tribal leaders who brought gifts at the dedication of the מזבח (במדבר 7).
Groups of ordinary Jews who stood alongside the קרבנות each week. Those who stayed home fasted, prayed, and read the Torah.

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'בתעניות —' is not a complete sentence. The משנה's answer for fast days continues on the next amud.

phrases.english: On Hanukkah: from the portion of the princes.
On Purim: "And Amalek came."
On the New Moons: "And on your new months."
In the watches: the act of Creation.
On fast days —
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list from the major festivals to the smaller special days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Minor holidays and special days also have fixed Torah readings that match their theme.
